chapter_name: Special Issues (Suicide, Sexual Dysfunction, Gender Dysphoria, AIDS, Paraphilic Disorders, Abuse, and Personality Disorders)
chapter_title: Special Issues (Suicide, Sexual Dysfunction, Gender Dysphoria, AIDS, Paraphilic Disorders, Abuse, and Personality Disorders)

questions.question_text: Which of the following sexual dysfunctions is least commonly associated with male sexual complaints?

options.text: Premature (early) ejaculation
Erectile disorder
Delayed ejaculation
Substance/medication-induced sexual dysfunction
Male hypoactive sexual desire disorder

correct_answer.text: Delayed ejaculation

correct_answers.text: Delayed ejaculation

questions.explanation: The prevalence of delayed ejaculation is unknown because of the lack of a precise definition of the syndrome, and it is the least common sexual complaint among men. The prevalence of all other male sexual dysfunctions is variable, and is strongly related to age factors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is not included under the category of sexual dysfunction in DSM-5?

options.text: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder
Delayed ejaculation
Female orgasmic disorder
Male orgasmic disorder
Female sexual interest/arousal disorder

correct_answer.text: Male orgasmic disorder

correct_answers.text: Male orgasmic disorder

questions.explanation: Male orgasmic disorder (used to be listed in DSM-IV) is no longer listed in DSM-5. All other conditions listed, along with male hypoactive sexual desire disorder, premature (early) ejaculation, and substance/medication-induced sexual dysfunction are all under the category of sexual dysfunction in DSM-5.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding gender dysphoria are accurate except:

options.text: In DSM-5 there are two different sets of diagnostic criteria for either gender dysphoria in children or gender dysphoria in adolescents and adults.
Latency-age boys with gender dysphoria express the wish to be a girl, prefer dressing in girls' clothes, and like to participate in traditionally feminine activities and games.
The specifier 'posttransition' is only available for gender dysphoria in adolescents and adults.
Latency-age natal girls with gender dysphoria express the wish to be a boy, prefer boys' clothing and hairstyles, and like to participate in contact sports and rough-and tumble play.
Younger children with this disorder are more likely than older ones to express extreme anatomic dysphoria.

correct_answer.text: Younger children with this disorder are more likely than older ones to express extreme anatomic dysphoria.

correct_answers.text: Younger children with this disorder are more likely than older ones to express extreme anatomic dysphoria.

questions.explanation: Older children, adolescents, and adults with this disorder are more likely than younger children to express extreme and persistent anatomic dysphoria.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the development and course of gender dysphoria are accurate except:

options.text: The onset of cross-gender behaviors occurs usually between ages 2 and 4 years during which time most children start expressing gendered behaviors and interests.
Some natal female children whose gender dysphoria does not persist become sexually attracted to females.
Few young children express anatomic dysphoria but it becomes a more common concern when approaching and anticipating puberty.
Natal males with late-onset gender dysphoria are mostly attracted to males and cohabit with natal males.
Most natal male children whose gender dysphoria does not persist become sexually attracted to males.

correct_answer.text: Natal males with late-onset gender dysphoria are mostly attracted to males and cohabit with natal males.

correct_answers.text: Natal males with late-onset gender dysphoria are mostly attracted to males and cohabit with natal males.

questions.explanation: Natal males with late-onset gender dysphoria are most likely to engage in transvestic behavior with sexual excitement, and are likely to be attracted by females and tend to cohabit with or are married to natal females.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is least likely to be associated with boys who have gender dysphoria?

options.text: Having more brothers than sisters
Avoidance of rough-and-tumble play activities
Birth later in the order in a multiple brother sibling-ship
Right-handedness
Low activity level

correct_answer.text: Right-handedness

correct_answers.text: Right-handedness

questions.explanation: Left-handedness is more common among boys with gender dysphoria.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are accurate regarding the study 'US National Longitudinal Lesbian Family Study: Psychological Adjustment of 17-year-old Adolescents' except:

options.text: The outcome measure used was Achenbach CBCL.
The results are based on ratings and reports by their mothers.
The objective of the study was to document the psychological adjustment of adolescents who were conceived through donor insemination and raised by the same lesbian mothers.
The study concluded that the index adolescents demonstrated fewer competencies and more behavioral problems than their peers in the normative American population.
The index children were followed until they reached 17 years old.

correct_answer.text: The study concluded that the index adolescents demonstrated fewer competencies and more behavioral problems than their peers in the normative American population.

correct_answers.text: The study concluded that the index adolescents demonstrated fewer competencies and more behavioral problems than their peers in the normative American population.

questions.explanation: This particular study is the longest running prospective longitudinal study of same sex parented families. The authors concluded that adolescents of both genders raised by lesbian mothers since conception demonstrated healthy psychological adjustment.

questions.question_text: All of the following are research findings of the study 'Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Adolescents School Victimization: Implications for Young Adult Health and Adjustment' except:

options.text: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT)-related school victimization is strongly associated with young adult mental health problems.
LGBT-related school victimization increases risk for STDs and HIV.
LGBT-related school victimization is strongly associated with substance use or abuse.
LGBT-related school victimization increases risk for suicidal ideation among males.
LGBT-related school victimization increases risk for depression.

correct_answer.text: LGBT-related school victimization is strongly associated with substance use or abuse.

correct_answers.text: LGBT-related school victimization is strongly associated with substance use or abuse.

questions.explanation: There is no strong association between LGBT-related school victimization and substance use or abuse. The authors concluded that reduction of LGBT-related school victimization would probably lead to a significant long-term health gain and reduction of health disparities for the LGBT population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is the strongest predictor of future suicide?

options.text: None of the above
History of suicidality
History of nonsuicidal self-injurious behavior
History of suicide attempt
History of suicidal ideation

correct_answer.text: History of suicide attempt

correct_answers.text: History of suicide attempt

questions.explanation: History of suicide attempt is the strongest predictor of future suicide.

questions.question_text: How many folds of increased risk could a loaded gun in the home lead to completed suicide?

options.text: 2-fold
30-fold
20-fold
10-fold
50-fold

correct_answer.text: 30-fold

correct_answers.text: 30-fold

questions.explanation: Availability of a firearm at home increases risk of completed suicide significantly, especially when the gun is loaded. One study shows a loaded gun increases by 30-fold the risk for completing suicide, even among youth with no apparent psychopathology.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding risk factors of completed suicide are accurate except:

options.text: Hopelessness seems to be an independent risk factor beyond its association with depression.
Studies find a link between perfectionism and completed suicide.
Among all the comorbid conditions, major mood disorders are the most strongly associated with completed suicide.
In older adolescents there is a higher risk of using more lethal means while being influenced by substances.
Other high-risk comorbid conditions may include disruptive, anxiety, and substance use disorders.

correct_answer.text: Studies find a link between perfectionism and completed suicide.

correct_answers.text: Studies find a link between perfectionism and completed suicide.

questions.explanation: Studies failed to find a link between perfectionism and completed suicide even though a perfectionism personality trait seems to be associated with suicide attempts in youth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least likely to be a biological factor associated with suicidality?

options.text: Increased 5-HT2A receptor binding of the serotonin metabolite 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid
Increased activity of brain-derived neurotropic factor in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus
Increased protein kinase A and C activity
Increased cortisol levels in the late evening hours
Down regulation of cAMP-response element binding protein (CREB)

correct_answer.text: Increased protein kinase A and C activity

correct_answers.text: Increased protein kinase A and C activity

questions.explanation: Among other factors listed, decreased protein kinase A and C activity is another biological factor that is associated with completed suicidality.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a protective factor linked to low suicidality?

options.text: Less leisure time spent together with parents
Religious affiliation
Clearer academic expectation from parents
Highly active parental supervision
Clearer behavioral expectation from parents

correct_answer.text: Less leisure time spent together with parents

correct_answers.text: Less leisure time spent together with parents

questions.explanation: A positive child-parent connection (such as leisure and meal times spent together, active parental supervision, clearer academic and behavioral expectation), school/academic success, prosocial peer interactions, and religious affiliation are all associated with a lower rate of suicidality.

questions.question_text: Which of the following components should not be included during the exploration of suicidal intent?

options.text: Belief about intent
Prevention of discovery
Communication of suicidal intent
Preparatory behavior
None of the above

correct_answer.text: None of the above

correct_answers.text: None of the above

questions.explanation: Belief about intent, preparatory behavior, prevention of discovery, and communication of suicidal intent are four components that should be explored during the evaluation of suicidal intent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding assessment of suicidality is least correct?

options.text: Nonsuicidal self-injurious behaviors should be separated from suicide attempt because they are involved in separate populations with different lethality and risks.
Suicidal intent, suicide plan, access to means, lethality, precipitants, motivation, and consequences should all be included as components during the assessment.
Interpersonal conflict or loss, legal disciplinary problems, and chronic and ongoing physical and sexual abuse can all be precipitants.
Suicidal ideation should be evaluated based on both severity (intent) and pervasiveness (frequency and intensity).
Naturally occurring environmental contingencies may reinforce suicidality.

correct_answer.text: Nonsuicidal self-injurious behaviors should be separated from suicide attempt because they are involved in separate populations with different lethality and risks.

correct_answers.text: Nonsuicidal self-injurious behaviors should be separated from suicide attempt because they are involved in separate populations with different lethality and risks.

questions.explanation: Nonsuicidal self-injurious behavior should be differentiated from a suicide attempt.

questions.question_text: Based on the study 'Clinical and Psychosocial Predictors of Suicide Attempts and Nonsuicidal Self-Injury in the Adolescent Depression Antidepressant and Psychotherapy Trial,' all of the following conclusions were reported except:

options.text: Hopelessness is an independent predictor of suicidal attempts over the follow-up period.
High suicidality, nonsuicidal self-injury, and poor family functioning at study entry are significant independent predictors of suicide attempts over the 28 weeks of follow-up.
Nonsuicidal self-injury is an independent predictor of nonsuicidal self-injury over the follow-up period.
Anxiety disorder at baseline is an independent predictor of nonsuicidal self-injury over the follow-up period.
Being younger and female at study entry is an independent predictor of nonsuicidal self-injury over the follow-up period.

correct_answer.text: Hopelessness is an independent predictor of suicidal attempts over the follow-up period.

correct_answers.text: Hopelessness is an independent predictor of suicidal attempts over the follow-up period.

questions.explanation: Hopelessness, anxiety disorder, and being younger and female are all independent predictors of nonsuicidal injury over the follow-up period, but not predictors of suicide attempts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding clinical management of adolescent suicidal behavior is not fully accurate?

options.text: Clinical interventions include safety planning, psychosocial treatment package, and hospitalization.
Removal of guns from the homes of at-risk adolescents is highly recommended.
Receiving written contact via postcard after discharge from hospital reduces reattempt.
Safety planning refers to negotiating a detailed written no-harm contract with the adolescent to prevent suicide.
Treatment of depression may not be sufficient to reduce suicide risk.

correct_answer.text: Safety planning refers to negotiating a detailed written no-harm contract with the adolescent to prevent suicide.

correct_answers.text: Safety planning refers to negotiating a detailed written no-harm contract with the adolescent to prevent suicide.

questions.explanation: Safety plans are the most critical components of clinical management of adolescent suicidality, which involve collaborative efforts among the clinician, patient, and family.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding psychotherapy approaches for treating youth suicidality are accurate based on the updated research except:

options.text: In one study (TADS, 2004), the combination of fluoxetine and CBT is associated with decreased suicidal ideation as compared to placebo.
Modified DBT was developed for use with suicidal adolescents to decrease the length of treatment.
Inpatient treatment with DBT for adolescents hospitalized for suicidal ideation or attempt reduces reattempts and rehospitalization as compared to the inpatient treatment without DBT.
Multisystemic therapy reduces the rates of reattempt as compared to usual care group.
Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) focuses on developing mindfulness, emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal skills.

correct_answer.text: Inpatient treatment with DBT for adolescents hospitalized for suicidal ideation or attempt reduces reattempts and rehospitalization as compared to the inpatient treatment without DBT.

correct_answers.text: Inpatient treatment with DBT for adolescents hospitalized for suicidal ideation or attempt reduces reattempts and rehospitalization as compared to the inpatient treatment without DBT.

questions.explanation: Inpatient treatment with and without DBT for adolescents hospitalized for suicidal ideation or attempt both reduce self-reported depression, suicidal ideation, and hopelessness in similar fashions, but there are no differences in reattempts, compliance with outpatient treatment, or rehospitalization.

questions.question_text: All of the following are risk factors for child fatalities caused by maltreatment except:

options.text: Non-European American ethnicity
Children under 3 years of age
Girls
Mother under 21 years of age
Product of multiple births

correct_answer.text: Girls

correct_answers.text: Girls

questions.explanation: Being a boy (not girl), under the age of 3 years, having a mother under the age of 21, being the product of a multiple birth, and non-European ethnicity are all risk factors for child fatalities due to maltreatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following reflect accurate epidemiological data available regarding sexual abuse except:

options.text: The most common age of initial sexual abuse is between 5 and 7 years.
Prior to the age of 18 years, 10–25% of girls are sexually victimized in some fashion.
Unrelated males are the most common perpetrator of sexual abuse against boys.
20% of cases are perpetrated by adolescents.
The most common perpetrators of sexual abuse against girls are male parents or male parent figures.

correct_answer.text: The most common age of initial sexual abuse is between 5 and 7 years.

correct_answers.text: The most common age of initial sexual abuse is between 5 and 7 years.

questions.explanation: The most common age of initial sexual abuse is 8–11 years.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the profiles of perpetrators of sexual abuse are correct except:

options.text: They are often described as passive and inadequate in most aspects of their life.
Selection of victimized children is based primarily on their sexual attraction.
The victims are considered as their narcissistic extensions.
Appearance and age of the victims may match their own characteristics when they were first abused.
They tend to put themselves into situations where children can be accessed.

correct_answer.text: Selection of victimized children is based primarily on their sexual attraction.

correct_answers.text: Selection of victimized children is based primarily on their sexual attraction.

questions.explanation: Perpetrators tend to select their victims primarily based more on their emotional needs than sexual attraction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the least common characteristic of physical abuse?

options.text: Rib fractures and spiral fractures
Multiple injuries at similar stages of healing
Head and eye injuries
Burns
Ruptured viscera

correct_answer.text: Multiple injuries at similar stages of healing

correct_answers.text: Multiple injuries at similar stages of healing

questions.explanation: Multiple injuries with various (not similar) stages of healing are more characteristic of physical abuse.

questions.question_text: All of the following are parts of a common constellation of clinical findings of whiplash shaken baby syndrome in infants and toddlers except:

options.text: Apparent external cranial trauma
Retinal hemorrhages
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
Subdural hemorrhage
None of the above

correct_answer.text: Apparent external cranial trauma

correct_answers.text: Apparent external cranial trauma

questions.explanation: Little or no evidence of external cranial trauma exists in whiplash shaken baby syndrome in infants and toddlers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following technologies should be considered as the first-line choice in assessing children with suspected acute brain or head injury?

options.text: Ultrasound
Bone scans
EEG
CT scanning
MRI

correct_answer.text: CT scanning

correct_answers.text: CT scanning

questions.explanation: CT scanning has high sensitivity to hemorrhage (intraparenchymal, subarachnoid, subdural, and epidural) and mass effect. Thus, CT scanning should be considered as the first-line choice over MRI or other technologies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the least likely sign of sexual abuse?

options.text: Anogenital injuries
Primary enuresis or encopresis
Redness or irritation of the vulva
Anal fissures or blood in the stool
Vague somatic complaints

correct_answer.text: Primary enuresis or encopresis

correct_answers.text: Primary enuresis or encopresis

questions.explanation: Secondary ( not primary) enuresis or encopresis could be a sign of sexual abuse in children among other signs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychiatric disorders and conditions is least commonly associated with childhood physical abuse?

options.text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
ADHD
PTSD
Aggression
Attachment dysregulation

correct_answer.text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder

correct_answers.text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder

questions.explanation: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is not commonly associated with physical abuse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the least likely outcome of sexual abuse in youth?

options.text: Sexual abuse and emotional abuse are independent risk factors for future engagement in sex trade work.
Overstimulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis leads to decreased cortisol levels.
Decreased hippocampus size is detected by MRI and PET scans in patients with PTSD due to severe sexual or physical abuse.
Long duration, use of force, penetration, and being victimized by perpetrators known to the victims are all associated with worse outcomes.
Dissociation may be temporarily protective, and may become maladaptive over time.

correct_answer.text: Overstimulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis leads to decreased cortisol levels.

correct_answers.text: Overstimulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis leads to decreased cortisol levels.

questions.explanation: Overstimulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis leads to increased cortisol levels.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements accurately describe the relationship between childhood maltreatment and substance/non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) except:

options.text: Head banging, self-mutilation, rocking, and other painful stimuli may activate endogenous opiates, which facilitates dissociation.
Both emotional abuse and sexual abuse have the strongest link to NSSI.
Alcohol activates the mesolimbic reward system in children deprived of true rewards in their lives.
Children with a maltreatment history are more likely to develop substance abuse as a way of self-medicating.
Emotional abuse leads to NSSI, which might be due to the development of self-critical cognitive style.

correct_answer.text: Alcohol activates the mesolimbic reward system in children deprived of true rewards in their lives.

correct_answers.text: Alcohol activates the mesolimbic reward system in children deprived of true rewards in their lives.

questions.explanation: Stimulants ( not alcohol) activate the mesolimbic dopaminergic reward system in children deprived of true rewards in their lives.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most predictive factor that is linked to resilience or lack of it based on Daigneault et al. (2007)?

options.text: Family violence
None of the above
Out-of-home placements
Interpersonal trust
Maternal conflicts

correct_answer.text: Interpersonal trust

correct_answers.text: Interpersonal trust

questions.explanation: Interpersonal trust is the most predictive of resilience.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding legal considerations during the evaluation of child maltreatment are correct except:

options.text: The most important factor is prompt report and referral to ensure appropriate collection and validation of data.
Confidential issues need to be clarified prior to a forensic evaluation.
Specific requirements and guidelines vary across different states.
The forensic evaluation and data collection should be completed by the treating provider who suspects the abuse.
All 50 states mandate physicians and mental health clinicians to report suspected child abuse to authorities.

correct_answer.text: The forensic evaluation and data collection should be completed by the treating provider who suspects the abuse.

correct_answers.text: The forensic evaluation and data collection should be completed by the treating provider who suspects the abuse.

questions.explanation: The forensic evaluation should be completed by a forensic-trained clinician separate from the treating provider who suspects the abuse.

questions.question_text: Which of the following types of child maltreatments may be most prevalent?

options.text: Physical abuse
Emotional maltreatment (psychological maltreatment)
Sexual assault
Neglect
Sexual abuse

correct_answer.text: Emotional maltreatment (psychological maltreatment)

correct_answers.text: Emotional maltreatment (psychological maltreatment)

questions.explanation: Emotional maltreatment (psychological maltreatment) may be the most prevalent form of child maltreatment, and may be the most likely to be underreported.

questions.question_text: Based on the 'Childhood Trauma and Children's Emerging Psychotic Symptoms: A Genetically Sensitive Longitudinal Cohort Study,' which of the following types of maltreatment is most associated with reporting psychotic symptoms?

options.text: Sexual abuse by parents
Neglect by caregivers
Emotional abuse by parents
Bullying by peers
Maltreatment by siblings

correct_answer.text: Bullying by peers

correct_answers.text: Bullying by peers

questions.explanation: Both bullying by peers and maltreatment by an adult with intent to harm are strongly associated with self-reported psychotic symptoms, which suggests intention to harm and perceived threat could be factors regardless of the forms of maltreatments per se.

questions.question_text: Based on the 'Childhood Trauma and Children's Emerging Psychotic Symptoms: A Genetically Sensitive Longitudinal Cohort Study,' which of the following childhood trauma factors is most strongly associated with reporting psychotic symptoms?

options.text: Forms of trauma
Timing of the trauma
Age of the victim
Sex of the victim
Accumulative effect

correct_answer.text: Accumulative effect

correct_answers.text: Accumulative effect

questions.explanation: The accumulative effect of abuse or trauma confers the highest risk for developing psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: According to the study 'Physical Punishment and Mental Disorders: Results From a Nationally Representative US Sample,' all of the following statements are accurate except:

options.text: The study investigates the relationship between harsh physical punishment and mental disorders.
The data is based on the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions between 2004 and 2005.
Harsh physical punishment is associated with increased odds of mood, anxiety, and substance use disorders.
Harsh physical punishment is not associated with increased odds of personality disorders
The study indicates that independent of other forms of child maltreatment harsh physical punishment is a risk factor for developing mental disorders.

correct_answer.text: Harsh physical punishment is not associated with increased odds of personality disorders

correct_answers.text: Harsh physical punishment is not associated with increased odds of personality disorders

questions.explanation: Youth and young adults with identity problems may be misperceived temporarily as having a personality disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following interventions for foster families are used to treat children during middle childhood except:

options.text: Attachment and Biobehavioral Catch-up (ABC)
Fostering Individualized Assistance Program (FIAP)
Middle School Success (MSS)
Incredible Years (IY)
Keeping Foster Parents Trained and Supported (KEEP)

correct_answer.text: Attachment and Biobehavioral Catch-up (ABC)

correct_answers.text: Attachment and Biobehavioral Catch-up (ABC)

questions.explanation: Middle School Success (MSS) is not listed as an intervention for treating children during middle childhood.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the epidemiology of HIV/AIDS in youth are accurate based on the latest data except:

options.text: Most female adolescents aged 13–19 are infected through heterosexual contact.
Black/African American youth constitute almost 70% of the cases for adolescents.
About three-fourths of male adolescent cases are transmitted through male-to-male sexual contact.
With nearly 1.2 million Americans infected with HIV/AIDS, pediatric AIDS is not uncommon.
Between 1994 and 2004 HIV/AIDS cases via maternal transmission decreased significantly.

correct_answer.text: With nearly 1.2 million Americans infected with HIV/AIDS, pediatric AIDS is not uncommon.

correct_answers.text: With nearly 1.2 million Americans infected with HIV/AIDS, pediatric AIDS is not uncommon.

questions.explanation: With nearly 1.2 million Americans infected with HIV/AIDS, pediatric AIDS is fortunately rare.

questions.question_text: The most common way by which a child acquires HIV/AIDS is:

options.text: Being born to a mother infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/AIDS
Homosexual activity with an HIV-infected person
Heterosexual activity with an HIV-infected person
Kissing an HIV-infected person
Receiving a blood transfusion

correct_answer.text: Being born to a mother infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/AIDS

correct_answers.text: Being born to a mother infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/AIDS

questions.explanation: The majority of pediatric HIV/AIDS cases are the result of children being born to mothers who have AIDS or are HIV positive.

questions.question_text: All of the following are possible neurological manifestations of HIV/AIDS except:

options.text: Peripheral neuropathy
Dementia
Seizure
Cerebral toxoplasmosis
Central nervous system lymphoma

correct_answer.text: Dementia

correct_answers.text: Dementia

questions.explanation: The term 'dementia' should not be commonly used to describe HIV-associated cognitive deficits. Instead, such cognitive deficits are commonly referred to as either 'HIV encephalopathy' or 'HIV-associated progressive encephalopathy.'

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the treatment of HIV/AIDS in youth are appropriate except:

options.text: A multidisciplinary approach is ideal.
Family-centered approaches are recommended.
The aim of antiretroviral medications is the eradication of viral replications.
Combination of multiple drugs under different categories is recommended.
Antiretroviral medications can help improve cognitive deficits caused by HIV-associated encephalopathy.

correct_answer.text: The aim of antiretroviral medications is the eradication of viral replications.

correct_answers.text: The aim of antiretroviral medications is the eradication of viral replications.

questions.explanation: The aim of antiretroviral medications is not the eradication of viral replications. Instead, the goal is to suppress viral replication, which usually requires a combination of multiple antiretroviral medications with different mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to have drug-drug interactions with certain psychotropic medications?

options.text: Emtricitabine
Didanosine
Abacavir
Zidovudine
Ritonavir

correct_answer.text: Ritonavir

correct_answers.text: Ritonavir

questions.explanation: As a protease inhibitor and a potent inhibitor of 3A4 and paninhibitors of other P450 isoenzymes ritonavir is most likely to have drug-drug interactions with certain psychotropic medications.

questions.question_text: Based on research data in adults which of the following antidepressants does not seem to lead to clinically significant drug-drug interactions with ritonavir?

options.text: Paroxetine
Sertraline
Fluoxetine
Escitalopram
Citalopram

correct_answer.text: Escitalopram

correct_answers.text: Escitalopram

questions.explanation: Based on research data from adults escitalopram does not seem to lead to clinically significant drug-drug interactions with ritonavir.

questions.question_text: Under the personality disorder section of DSM-5, there are 10 specific personality disorders included. Which of the following is not one of them?

options.text: Borderline personality disorder
Antisocial personality disorder
Passive-aggressive personality disorder
Schizoid personality disorder
Histrionic personality disorder

correct_answer.text: Passive-aggressive personality disorder

correct_answers.text: Passive-aggressive personality disorder

questions.explanation: Passive-aggressive personality is not listed as a formal personality disorder in DSM-5. However, it can be considered under 'other specified personality disorder and unspecified personality disorder' if the individual meets the general criteria for a personality disorder.

questions.question_text: According to DSM-5, all of the following personality disorders can be potentially assigned to individuals under the age of 18 years except:

options.text: Obsessive personality disorder
Schizotypal personality disorder
Narcissistic personality disorder
Dependent personality disorder
Antisocial personality disorder

correct_answer.text: Antisocial personality disorder

correct_answers.text: Antisocial personality disorder

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the only personality disorder that has an age diagnostic requirement in DSM-5 (at least age 18 years).

questions.question_text: What is the minimal duration of symptoms of personality disorders that must be present in order to diagnose personality disorders in individuals younger than 18 years?

options.text: Two years
One year
Five years
Three months
Six months

correct_answer.text: One year

correct_answers.text: One year

questions.explanation: Personality disorder diagnoses can be given in individuals younger than 18 years (except for antisocial personality disorder). However, the symptoms must be present for more than one year.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding borderline personality disorder are accurate except:

options.text: Core features include instability in relationships, self-image, and affects.
About 10% of individuals with borderline personality disorder complete suicide.
It is often associated with emotional dysregulation.
The disorder shows significant impairment and risk of self-harm.
Prevalence of this disorder is higher in older age groups than in the young adult group.

correct_answer.text: Prevalence of this disorder is higher in older age groups than in the young adult group.

correct_answers.text: Prevalence of this disorder is higher in older age groups than in the young adult group.

questions.explanation: The prevalence of borderline personality disorder decreases as people age, and is lower in the older age groups.

questions.question_text: All of the following biological findings based on neuroimaging studies are associated with borderline personality disorder except:

options.text: Dysfunction of anterior cingulate cortex, orbitofrontal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex
Bilateral increases in activation of the amygdala in response to affective stimuli
Dysfunction of frontal-limbic network
Increased left amygdala activation to facial expression of emotion
Increased amygdala and hippocampal volume

correct_answer.text: Increased amygdala and hippocampal volume

correct_answers.text: Increased amygdala and hippocampal volume

questions.explanation: Decreased amygdala and hippocampal volume is found in patients with borderline disorder by structural MRI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following should be excluded from the potential psychosocial factors for youth developing borderline personality disorder?

options.text: Serious parental psychopathology
None
History of neglect
History of separation from primary caregivers
History of trauma (physical abuse, sexual abuse, and other maltreatment)

correct_answer.text: None

correct_answers.text: None

questions.explanation: None of the listed factors should be excluded as psychosocial risk factors for developing borderline personality disorder.

questions.question_text: In comparison of the prevalence rates of comorbid conditions between youth with borderline personality disorder and those without, which of the following conditions is significantly more prevalent in youth with borderline personality disorder?

options.text: Conduct disorder
Major depressive disorder
ADHD
Oppositional defiant disorder
Separation anxiety disorder

correct_answer.text: Conduct disorder

correct_answers.text: Conduct disorder
